No content relevant to any Chapter 5B question.","exclusion_reason":"Page navigation boilerplate containing only structural elements: language selector, menu links, publisher information, and metadata fields. No substantive biographical or policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0004"],"explanation":"Covers 2018 electoral platform themes including pursuit of broad-based prosperity over neoliberal rents (5B.1), social focus on poor and indigenous communities (5B.8), opposition to 'neoporfirist regime' of corruption (5B.5, 5B.7), and rejection of 'falsa alternancia' implying lack of fair competition rules (5B.4). Contains early career background on indigenous community work relevant to economic exclusion (5B.2). Unit-0002 provides the ideological frame for the 2018 economic agenda.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0002","unit-0004"],"explanation":"2006 electoral dispute: López Obrador contested results with 0.56% margin, claimed 'robo' (theft) of election, launched civil disobedience, proclaimed himself 'legitimate president.' Evidence bearing on 5B.7 (reliable economic information — he rejected official electoral results as fraudulent), 5B.1 (short-term popularity vs broad-based prosperity — his response prioritized political loyalty/consumption over accepting institutional results), and 5B.9 (shock management — his response to the electoral shock was political mobilization rather than institutional correction).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0005"],"explanation":"Covers 2012 defeat, Peña Nieto victory, López Obrador's founding of MORENA, rejection of the bipartisan 'Pacto por México,' and systematic opposition to EPN's structural reforms (energy, education, labor, telecommunications). Evidence for 5B.3 (he opposed fiscal/energy rules that protected macroeconomic stability), 5B.4 (opposed competition/trade/investment rules as threats to sovereignty), 5B.5 (his anti-corruption framing), 5B.7 (denied legitimacy of the regime's economic information), 5B.9 (response to what he characterized as economic shocks from EPN policies), 5B.10 (trajectory judgment — he claimed EPN left worse trajectory).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0004","unit-0006"],"explanation":"The 2018 campaign program (Juntos Haremos Historia coalition) is described in detail: 'austeridad republicana' reorienting resources from current spending to investment without tax increases (5B.1, 5B.3), addressing social causes and poverty (5B.8), increasing domestic gasoline production to reduce imports and prices (5B.4, 5B.9), energy and food self-sufficiency (5B.4, 5B.10), combating corruption 'giving example' from Los Pinos (5B.5, 5B.7), support for migrants during Trump shocks (5B.9). This is the most comprehensive economic policy statement for the governing period.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Describes the 2018-2024 government platform as 'pragmatic socialdemocracy' that accepts free market principles, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, and peso flotation while rejecting privatization and prioritizing national production (5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4). Explicitly promises not to jail Peña Nieto — indicating capture/anti-corruption rule limitation (5B.5). More conservative stance on abortion and same-sex marriage — relevant to distributional equity across groups (5B.8). December 2018 inauguration with National Guard, peace plan, amnesty consideration (5B.9).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Covers transitional period in late 2018: USMCA trade deal approval, migration caravans at the US-Mexico border, Trump threats to close border. Contains marginal content on trade (USMCA as beneficial per López Obrador) and migration policy, but these are pre-presidency events rather than governing economic decisions. The substantive economic governance content begins in unit-0006.","exclusion_reason":"Trade deal referenced is a pre-presidency approval of USMCA already finalized before López Obrador took office; migration border tensions are foreign policy context rather than domestic economic governance. No enacted budgets, fiscal rules, qualified appointments, anti-corruption enforcement, or economic trajectory assessment."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Table of contents/structural navigation for the biography. No substantive content on economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Enumerates section headings 1-10 of the biography for navigation purposes. Contains no policy content, factual claims about economic management, or governance outcomes relevant to any 5B question."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Early biography from birth through 1969 family tragedy and relocation. No content on economic governance, policy positions, or ruler effectiveness.","exclusion_reason":"Childhood biography covering family background, early schooling, baseball, Catholic altar boy service, and 1969 accidental death of younger brother José Ramón. No content relevant to economic governance questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Political socialization at UNAM (1972) and early party activism within PRI system. No economic governance content relevant to the 5B questions about ruling-period performance.","exclusion_reason":"University enrollment in Political Science at UNAM and initial PRI party activism from 1976 onwards. No enacted policies, budgets, appointments, or economic governance decisions relevant to Chapter 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Career in Tabasco state government functions (INI delegation, COPLAMAR, university teaching), marriage to Rocío Beltrán, first book publication. No relevant economic governance content for the 5B framework.","exclusion_reason":"Early state government positions in Tabasco dealing with indigenous communities and agricultural programs, university teaching, marriage, and publication of a historical book on Tabasco. All pre-governance-period biographical content with no direct bearing on 5B economic management questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"1988 election campaigns within FDN coalition and creation of PRD. No economic governance content — the elections described are opposition electoral contests, not governing-period economic decisions.","exclusion_reason":"1988 presidential and gubernatorial electoral campaigns in Tabasco under the FDN coalition. No enacted policies, appointments, fiscal rules, or economic governance decisions. The electoral fraud allegations concern opposition campaigns rather than ruling-period economic management."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Creation of PRD in May 1989 and 'exodus for democracy' march of 1991-1992. No economic governance content relevant to ruling-period performance.","exclusion_reason":"PRD founding and the 1991-1992 'exodus for democracy' march from Tabasco to Mexico City. These are opposition political activities predating any governorship. No enacted economic policies, fiscal rules, anti-corruption enforcement, or budget decisions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Second failed gubernatorial bid in Tabasco (1994), Zedillo election context, PRD electoral defeat. No enacted economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Second gubernatorial campaign in Tabasco ending in defeat, electoral context of Zedillo's presidency and PRI internal conflicts, PRD losses. These are opposition electoral activities with no enacted governing-period economic decisions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"López Obrador's election as PRD party president in July 1996 with 73.9% of votes. Internal party governance only, not national economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Election to PRD party presidency following PRD electoral defeats and internal turmoil. Party leadership is not national economic governance; no enacted fiscal, tax, monetary, competition, anti-corruption, or budget policies at the national level."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PRD electoral victories of 1997 (Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas winning DF mayoralty), PRD gains in Legislative Assembly and Chamber of Deputies, PRD victories in three additional states by 1999. Opposition party-building context.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition party electoral successes in 1997-1999 at state and federal levels. These describe opposition party performance in elections, not enacted national economic governance by López Obrador. No national fiscal rules, budgets, appointments, anti-corruption enforcement, or economic trajectory."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"López Obrador's primary election as PRD candidate for DF mayor (November 1999), research published on FOBAPROA banking rescue fund. The FOBAPROA content is anti-corruption/anti-privatization critique as opposition figure, not governing-period evidence.","exclusion_reason":"DF mayoral primary candidacy and opposition critique of FOBAPROA. No governing-period economic decisions by López Obrador. FOBAPROA critique is opposition political stance, not enacted economic governance during his own rule."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0017","unit-0019"],"explanation":"López Obrador wins DF mayoralty with 34.5% in July 2000, describing his first electoral mandate. Vicente Fox wins presidency. This establishes his first governance position, the DF government. While not national-level, it is his first governing-period and relevant to baseline trajectory questions. His governing agenda included infrastructure and social programs (unit-0019 begins coverage).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0018","unit-0020"],"explanation":"DF government 2000-2005 period: vigorous public works campaign, social protection programs including Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores, commitment to accountability and transparency. Opposition PAN accusation of populism and fiscal mismanagement. Relevant to 5B.1 (prosperity agenda vs patronage), 5B.6 (infrastructure vs announcements), 5B.7 (transparency and accountability claims), 5B.8 (social programs for elderly), 5B.10 (trajectory from predecessor). Unit-0020 continues DF governance assessment.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0019","unit-0021"],"explanation":"DF governance assessment continuing: characterization of López Obrador as 'Peje' pejelagarto and 'AMLO.' Describes intensive public works and social programs (Pensión Alimenticia), morning press conferences (las mañaneras) as transparency mechanism. Also covers his PNR (公民) governance achievements and polarization. Directly relevant to 5B.6 (infrastructure quality), 5B.7 (transparency via morning press), 5B.8 (social transfers). Unit-0021 continues.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0020","unit-0022"],"explanation":"DF governance results: vigorous infrastructure campaign, social programs especially for the elderly (Pensión Universal Alimenticia), resistance to implementing Seguro Popular on grounds that DF already provided free coverage. PAN criticism of populist spending and rising debts. Criminal violence management results. Relevant to 5B.1 (broad prosperity vs patronage), 5B.6 (infrastructure quality), 5B.7 (transparency), 5B.8 (social distribution). Unit-0022 begins the videoescándalo section.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0021","unit-0023"],"explanation":"March 2004 videoescándalo: Televisa broadcasts clandestine videos of López Obrador's closest collaborators (Gustavo Ponce Meléndez, René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz) gambling in Las Vegas casinos and negotiating corrupt payments with businessman Carlos Ahumada Kurtz. This is directly relevant to 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement against politically connected actors) and 5B.7 (reliable economic/governance information — his collaborators were caught lying about corrupt dealings).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0022","unit-0024"],"explanation":"López Obrador's response to videoescándalo: tardy and mild rejection of the corrupt practices, emphasized political conspiracy by ex-president Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and Fox. Rosario Robles forced to leave PRD. His reaction is evidence for 5B.5 (failure to enforce anti-corruption rules against politically connected actors in his own administration) and 5B.7 (denial and scapegoating rather than acknowledging failures).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Desafuero process beginning May 2004: PGR seeks congressional permission to arrest López Obrdor over a minor land dispute in Cuajimalpa from 2000. Legal/judicial process, not economic governance. The underlying case was about a minor expropriation dispute, not an economic policy matter.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero legal process initiated by PGR over alleged abuse of authority in a Cuajimalpa land expropriation case. This is a judicial/constitutional conflict unrelated to economic governance. The land dispute was a minor administrative matter predating any broader economic policy framework. No enacted fiscal, monetary, competition, anti-corruption, or budget policies."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"2004 desafuero process continuing: 200,000 PRD supporters demonstrate in Zócalo, López Obrador presents alternative nation project book, Fox dismisses Marcelo Ebrard from security post following Tláhuac lynching incident. Pre-presidential electoral positioning and street mobilization.","exclusion_reason":"Continued desafuero controversy including mass demonstrations and publication of political book (March 2018 is different). The Fox administration's removal of Ebrard is executive decision by Fox, not López Obrador. These are pre-presidential political positioning events."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"April 2005 congressional vote approving desafuero by 360-127; López Obrador mobilizes civil resistance, Supreme Court intervention on constitutional immunity. Judicial/constitutional process, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"April 2005 congressional vote on desafuero and subsequent civil resistance mobilization. This is a constitutional/judicial dispute about immunity from prosecution, not an economic governance matter. No enacted fiscal, monetary, competition, anti-corruption, or budget policies."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"May 2005: PGR fails to get judge to initiate proceedings; Fox accepts prosecutor Macedo de la Concha's resignation; charges dropped; Fox meets López Obrador. Political resolution of judicial conflict, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Resolution of desafuero conflict through political negotiation resulting in charges being dropped and Fox-López Obrador meeting. This is a political settlement of a judicial dispute, not an economic governance outcome. No enacted fiscal, monetary, anti-corruption, or budget policies."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"July 2005 López Obrador requests leave from DF government to focus on PRD presidential primary. Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas withdraws from race. September 2005 designated as PRD presidential candidate. Pre-presidential campaign activities.","exclusion_reason":"Leave of absence from DF government and PRD presidential primary candidacy designation. These are pre-presidential campaign activities and party nomination procedures, not enacted economic governance during a presidential term."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"2006 presidential campaign: candidate profiles (Calderón, Madrazo), PAN attacks warning López Obrador would 'hundir' (sink) the country with heterodox economics. Electoral campaign content, not governing-period economic decisions.","exclusion_reason":"Pre-election presidential campaign narrative covering candidate profiles and PAN's anti-AMLO advertising campaign. Electoral campaign content is pre-governance positioning, not enacted economic governance decisions. PAN's characterization of his economic policies as dangerous is opposition campaign rhetoric, not evidence of his actual economic management."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0029","unit-0031"],"explanation":"2006 PRD campaign program (Coalición por el Bien de Todos): eliminating corruption 'from top to bottom' (5B.5), austerity including halving presidential salary (5B.1, 5B.3), social programs extending services to deprived areas and vulnerable populations (5B.8), opposition to FOBAPROA privatization, proposal for Truth Commission (5B.5, 5B.7). Economic agenda explicitly: fight tax fraud and evasion, redirect savings to social and productive programs (agriculture, tourism, public works) (5B.6). This is the first comprehensive economic policy program.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0030","unit-0032"],"explanation":"2006 campaign program continuation: energy sector — only efficiency improvements, no privatization of Pemex (5B.3, 5B.4), constitutional right to 'fair' and 'dignified' minimum wage without specifying amount (5B.8), opposition to NAFTA agricultural terms, prioritization of migration and border relations with US (5B.9). Social programs funded by austerity savings (5B.1, 5B.6). Evidence of economic platform for 2018-2024 agenda.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"López Obrador's explicit distancing from Chávez and Venezuela. International relations/foreign policy content, not domestic economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"López Obrador explicitly denies any connection to Chávez or Venezuelan government, distinguishing his 'mexicanismo' as 'ni chavismo, ni trumpismo.' This is foreign policy positioning, not domestic economic governance. No enacted fiscal rules, anti-corruption enforcement, budget allocation, or economic trajectory assessment."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0032","unit-0034"],"explanation":"July 2006 election night: tight initial count placing López Obrador ahead by up to 1 million votes, then PREP reversal giving Calderón 0.64% lead. EU observation mission dismissed fraud. Electoral administration and information reliability (5B.7). López Obrador's subsequent refusal to accept official count as evidence of information credibility dispute (5B.7). Also 5B.9 — shock from perceived electoral fraud and his mobilization response.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0033","unit-0035"],"explanation":"After TEPJF validates Calderón win (August-September 2006), López Obrador escalates: declares IFE, Fox, and Calderón as 'ariete,' 'traidor,' and 'pelele' respectively. Calls for civil resistance, blocks Congress, refuses to recognize results.
